note: Bilstein 6112 fronts at $449 plus an SCS add-a-leaf at $189, good for 1.5 to 2 inches.
Five Falken Wildpeak 285/75R16 at about $215 each; at 2 inches trim the mud flap bracket, and 2.5 inches clears untouched.
CBI frame-mounted sliders at $699; a nerf step is not a substitute.
CBI kit covers oil pan, transmission, transfer case and fuel tank; check for crossmember gussets.
A steel hybrid adds about 120 pounds, so set the 6112 collars for it; on 2018 and newer trucks, confirm it clears the Safety Sense radar.
Smittybilt X2O Gen2 10K on synthetic line; it needs the bumper's frame-tied winch mount.
A rated frame-mount point at the rear, since almost no Tacoma has one; never use a tow ball.
Icon Stage 2 with upper control arms; a lift past 2 inches runs out of caster without them, and the alignment is part of the cost.
Low end of the guide's $2,500 to $4,000 shop price; 4.88 for 33s and 5.29 for 35s, front and rear matched.
ARB at $1,250 plus a $400 compressor, an estimate. Skip on a TRD Off-Road, TRD Pro or 2022 and newer Trail Edition, which have a factory locker.
CBI bare bumper at about $1,150; a swing-out carrier adds $400 to $900 and makes the leaf pack upgrade required.
Total Chaos long-travel kit with 12 to 14 inches of front travel; a shop install, and a rear coilover conversion adds $2,000 to $4,000.
Five 35s at about $420 each plus about $200 in cab mount parts and welding you quote locally. Sources disagree on the lift, and the guide shows the range.
